Definition: from the oblique cases of G1473 (G1698, G1700, G1691); my:--of me, mine (own), my.
BiblicalUsage: Emos is 'my' or 'mine own' — the possessive that marks something as belonging to the speaker. Paul says he baptized no one in his own name in 1 Corinthians 1:15, calls God as a record upon his soul in 2 Corinthians 1:23, and signs off with the salutation of Paul with mine own hand in 2 Thessalonians 3:17. Peter looks ahead to his own decease in 2 Peter 1:15 and wants the churches to remember these things after he is gone.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'mine own' is a word of responsibility — Paul owns his words, his handwriting, and his name, and he will answer for them. I hold that what is truly mine is what I will stand behind before God, and that is why I want my own words to be few and true.
